text: The current Cocoa graphics state over a QPainter (R032). Cocoa draws through an implicit current context with a transform (CTM), a fill and stroke colour, and a save/restore stack. Here that state lives in Python: affine transforms are 6-tuples (m11, m12, m21, m22, tx, ty) composed with plain arithmetic, and a QTransform is built only when a shape is painted (no arithmetic on PythonQt wrappers; unary minus on them crashes FontLab). The base transform maps the drawing space (glyph units, or a view's y-up coordinates) to widget pixels. A context exists only inside a scope ( paint_scope for editor painters, view_scope for NSView.drawRect_ ). text: Glyph-editor painters on FontLab's native canvas hooks (resolves R054). Builds with flCanvas.appendPythonPainter(callback, order) call Python inside the canvas paint: UnderOwner before the glyphs are drawn, OverOwner after them. callback(painter, canvas) gets a painter that FontLab has saved and reset to viewport pixels; it is valid only during the call, so this module never creates or ends one. Both phases work, so a Reporter background is really drawn under the outlines.
